rows.title: Nonprofits say poor CT families missed $120 million in tax relief
rows.standfirst: An estimated 45,000 low-income Connecticut families failed to claim their full federal income tax benefits three years ago.

rows.title: Will Trump win spur CT to cut taxes on working families?
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont pledged to address ‘pocketbook issues,’ but that doesn’t necessarily mean Democrats will look to cut taxes next spring.

rows.title: Projected tax revenues surge, but CT can’t spend most of windfall
rows.standfirst: The ‘guardrails’ require that legislators save $2.5B in the next biennial budget, and the revenues they can spend grew by only around $620M.

rows.title: Lamont moves to tighten CT spending despite projected surplus
rows.standfirst: Despite a projected surplus, Lamont is ordering mid-year budget cuts to higher education while warning all agencies to tighten their belts.

rows.title: Lamont warns ‘fixed costs’ will consume all revenue growth in next CT budget
rows.standfirst: The budget analysis means it’s unlikely more money will be available for education, social services and other core programs.

rows.title: Lt. Gov Bysiewicz talks budgets, affordability at ‘In the Room’
rows.standfirst: For CT Mirror’s ‘In the Room’ series, Bysiewicz talked about officials’ efforts to control the state’s finances and pay down its debt.

rows.title: CT’s $8K per person in bonded debt leads the nation, report finds
rows.standfirst: CT’s bonded debt per person is over four times the national average, which the Lamont administration says illustrates the need for ‘sound fiscal management.’

rows.title: Lamont seeks more borrowing for transportation rebuild
rows.standfirst: CT plans to sell $1.3B in bonds for transportation projects next year, but the Lamont administration has missed borrowing targets before.
